## Welcome

The Doctoral Urban Planning seminar is a platform for the intellectual development of PhD students in the Department of Urban & Regional Planning. The seminar provides a shared space for students to present their research and to solicit critical, yet constructive, peer reviews and advice.





## The Seminar Cycle

The seminar is built around a **four-semester cycle** of workshops. Students cycle through all four phases during their pre-candidacy coursework.

## This Semester at a Glance

**Fall 2026: Writing Your First Article**

- **Fridays, 9:00–10:20 a.m. · TBH 111 Conference Room** — August 28 – December  4, 2026

- 7 workshop sessions — including article writing, journal targeting, argumentation, peer review, and co-authorship
- 4 rounds of peer presentations — informal, low-stakes research-in-progress talks
- ACSP conference prep in Week 6; no seminar Week 7 during the conference
- Annual CV check-in built into Week 1

**Spring 2027: Writing Your Dissertation Proposal**

- **Fridays, 9:00–10:20 a.m. · TBH 111 Conference Room** — January 22 – April 30, 2027
- 6 workshop sessions — including proposal structure, theoretical frameworks, methods, timelines, and defense strategies
- 4 milestone presentations — Plan of Study, updated plans, and QRP/Exam content
- ICUA/UAA presentation practice in Week 12; no seminar Week 13 during the conference
